The Woman.name: The Woman
The Woman.description: The woman is a character who took bed-curtains from a deceased person, discussing it with Joe. | The woman is a character who speaks boldly and challenges the others, sitting in a flaunting manner. | The woman is one of the speakers in the dialogue who argues that the dead man is not worse off for the loss of his possessions and engages in the transaction with Old Joe. | The Woman is a character who has taken a shirt from a deceased person's body to prevent it from being wasted, and she discusses the value of the items.

Tim.name: Tim
Tim.description: Tim is a character mentioned in an illustration description as a blood-horse all the way from church.

Cornhill.name: Cornhill
Cornhill.description: Cornhill is a place where Bob Cratchit went down a slide, likely a street in London. | Cornhill is a street in London where the clerk slides down on Christmas Eve after work.

Christmas Eve.name: Christmas Eve
Christmas Eve.description: Christmas Eve is an event mentioned as the reason for Bob Cratchit's slide on Cornhill. | Christmas Eve is the specific day on which the narrative takes place, setting a contrast between the festive season and Scrooge's demeanor.

The Three Spirits.name: The Three Spirits
The Three Spirits.description: The Three Spirits is a concept referring to the spirits in the story, with staves dedicated to each.

The End of It.name: The End of It
The End of It.description: The End of It is a concept representing the conclusion of the story, as titled in Stave Five.

Stave One.name: Stave One
Stave One.description: Stave One is the first chapter of the narrative, titled 'Marley's Ghost'.

Stave Two.name: Stave Two
Stave Two.description: Stave Two is a chapter of the narrative, referenced in the contents with a heading.

Stave Three.name: Stave Three
Stave Three.description: Stave Three is a chapter of the narrative, referenced in the contents with a heading.

Stave Four.name: Stave Four
Stave Four.description: Stave Four is a chapter of the narrative, referenced in the contents with a heading.

Stave Five.name: Stave Five
Stave Five.description: Stave Five is the final chapter of the narrative, referenced in the contents with a heading.

Burial Register.name: Burial Register
Burial Register.description: The burial register is a document that records the burial of Marley, signed by multiple parties.

Clergyman.name: Clergyman
Clergyman.description: The clergyman was one of the signatories of Marley's burial register.

Clerk.name: Clerk
Clerk.description: The clerk was one of the signatories of Marley's burial register. | The clerk is an employee of Scrooge who is described as cold but warmer than Scrooge, returning greetings cordially. He earns fifteen shillings a week and has a wife and family. | An employee at the counting-house who is given Christmas day off, goes down a slide, and runs home to Camden Town.

Undertaker.name: Undertaker
Undertaker.description: The undertaker was one of the signatories of Marley's burial register.

Chief Mourner.name: Chief Mourner
Chief Mourner.description: The chief mourner was one of the signatories of Marley's burial register.

Scrooge and Marley.name: Scrooge and Marley
Scrooge and Marley.description: Scrooge and Marley is the name of the firm that was known after Marley's death, with the name never being painted out. | Scrooge and Marley is the firm name displayed above the warehouse door, reflecting the partnership between Scrooge and the deceased Marley.

Hamlet's Father.name: Hamlet's Father
Hamlet's Father.description: Hamlet's father is a character from Shakespeare's play who died before the play begins, used as a comparison to emphasize the certainty of Marley's death.

St. Paul's Churchyard.name: St. Paul's Churchyard
St. Paul's Churchyard.description: St. Paul's Churchyard is a breezy spot mentioned as a setting for a hypothetical stroll by a middle-aged gentleman.

Paul's Churchyard.name: Paul's Churchyard
Paul's Churchyard.description: Paul's Churchyard is a location referenced as an example of a place that might astonish Scrooge's son's weak mind.

Warehouse Door.name: Warehouse Door
Warehouse Door.description: The warehouse door is part of the business premises, above which the name 'Scrooge and Marley' is displayed.

The City Clocks.name: The City Clocks
The City Clocks.description: The City Clocks are timekeeping devices in the city that indicate it is three o'clock in the afternoon on Christmas Eve.

Fog.name: Fog
Fog.description: Fog is a dense atmospheric condition that envelops the streets and buildings on Christmas Eve, contributing to the gloomy setting. | The fog is a dense fog that envelops the city on Christmas Eve, making the houses opposite appear as mere phantoms and pouring in through chinks and keyholes. | Fog is a weather condition present in the scene, contributing to the cold and frosty atmosphere.

Counting-House.name: Counting-House
Counting-House.description: The Counting-House is Scrooge's workplace, where he sits busy on Christmas Eve, reflecting his dedication to business over personal connections. | The counting-house is Scrooge's place of business where he sits busy on Christmas Eve. It has a door open to keep an eye on the clerk, and it contains a fire and a coal-box. | A business office where Scrooge works and shuts up at the end of the day. | The counting-house is the place of business associated with Scrooge and Marley, which the Ghost's spirit never roved beyond during life.

Scrooge's Clerk.name: Scrooge's Clerk
Scrooge's Clerk.description: The clerk is an employee in Scrooge's counting-house, working in a small cell copying letters. He has a very small fire and tries to warm himself at a candle. | Scrooge's clerk is an employee of Scrooge, mentioned in Scrooge's wish to speak to him.

Scrooge's Nephew.name: Scrooge's Nephew
Scrooge's Nephew.description: Scrooge's nephew is a cheerful young man who visits Scrooge on Christmas Eve and greets him with 'A merry Christmas, uncle! God save you!' He is described as having a ruddy and handsome face. | Scrooge's nephew is a character who is cheerful and merry, and he visits Scrooge to wish him a Merry Christmas. | Scrooge's nephew is a kind and generous character who advocates for the true spirit of Christmas, emphasizing its potential for goodwill and human connection. | Scrooge's nephew is a cheerful and persistent character who invites his uncle to dine with him on Christmas, despite his uncle's refusal. | Scrooge's nephew is a cheerful individual who greets Scrooge with Christmas and New Year wishes, and treats the clerk cordially. | Scrooge's nephew, named Fred, is a jovial man who laughs heartily and celebrates Christmas with his wife and friends, and he criticizes Scrooge for calling Christmas a humbug. | Scrooge's nephew is Fred, a character who defends Scrooge and jokes about his beliefs regarding Christmas. | Scrooge's nephew is a relative of Scrooge who expresses pity rather than anger toward Scrooge, noting that Scrooge suffers from his own whims and misses out on a good dinner. | Scrooge's nephew is a good-natured individual who enjoys laughing and is determined to give Scrooge a chance every year, despite Scrooge's attitude. | Scrooge's nephew is the person who visits Uncle Scrooge every year, expressing goodwill and hoping to influence him positively. | Scrooge's nephew is a character who is part of the party and is implied to be in collusion with Topper regarding Topper's pretended blindness. | Scrooge's nephew is a character who hosts the games and finds amusement in Scrooge's participation.

Christmas.name: Christmas
Christmas.description: Christmas is an annual holiday that Scrooge criticizes as a humbug and a time of financial burden and aging. | Christmas is a holiday that Scrooge despises and his nephew cherishes, seen as a time for kindness and charity. | Christmas is the time of year when the charitable gentlemen choose to collect donations for the poor. | Christmas is the season during which the events of the story take place. | Christmas is the festive occasion during which the Cratchit family celebrates with a toast and blessings. | Christmas is a holiday that Scrooge dismisses as a humbug, sparking discussion among his relatives. | Christmas is a holiday that is central to the conversation, with Scrooge's nephew determined to visit Scrooge every year regardless of Scrooge's reaction. | Christmas is an annual holiday celebrated with family gatherings, games, and music. | Christmas is a holiday celebrated with merriment and goodwill, and the narrative suggests that the holiday season seems condensed into the time Scrooge spends with the Ghost. | The Christmas season is referenced as a background event during the family gathering. | Christmas is the holiday that Scrooge celebrates joyfully, reflecting his newfound spirit of generosity. | Christmas is a holiday that Scrooge is said to know how to keep well.

Frost.name: Frost
Frost.description: Frost is a weather condition present in the scene, contributing to the cold atmosphere.

The Clerk.name: The Clerk
The Clerk.description: The clerk is an employee in Scrooge's office who involuntarily applauds the nephew's speech, then suppresses his enthusiasm out of fear of Scrooge's reaction. | The clerk works for Scrooge and is poorly dressed for winter. He celebrates Christmas Eve by sliding on Cornhill and playing blind man's-buff at home in Camden Town.

Bedlam.name: Bedlam
Bedlam.description: Bedlam is referenced by Scrooge as a place he would retire to, implying a mental asylum, used metaphorically to express his disdain for the clerk's Christmas cheer.

Portly Gentlemen.name: Portly Gentlemen
Portly Gentlemen.description: The portly gentlemen are two pleasant visitors who enter Scrooge's office after his nephew leaves, carrying books and papers, and address the firm as Scrooge and Marley's.

Scrooge and Marley's.name: Scrooge and Marley's
Scrooge and Marley's.description: Scrooge and Marley's is the name of the business firm, as referred to by the portly gentlemen. | Scrooge and Marley's is the counting-house where Scrooge works, as referenced by The Gentleman when he identifies Scrooge.

Mr. Marley.name: Mr. Marley
Mr. Marley.description: Mr. Marley is a deceased partner of Scrooge, having been dead for seven years, as stated by Scrooge. | Mr. Marley is the deceased business partner of Mr. Scrooge, mentioned as having died seven years prior.

Mr. Scrooge.name: Mr. Scrooge
Mr. Scrooge.description: Mr. Scrooge is a character who is questioned by a gentleman about his identity and expresses skepticism about provisions for the poor. | Mr. Scrooge is described as an odious, stingy, hard, and unfeeling man, and is considered the Ogre of the Cratchit family.

The Gentleman.name: The Gentleman
The Gentleman.description: The Gentleman is a visitor who seeks donations for the poor and destitute during the festive season. | The Gentleman is a person who, along with others, is trying to raise funds to provide the poor with necessities and discusses their cause with Scrooge. | The Gentleman is a portly, good-natured individual who had visited Scrooge's counting-house the previous day to collect a charitable donation, and is now greeted warmly by Scrooge. | The gentleman is a person who initially addresses Scrooge, is surprised by Scrooge's offer, and agrees to visit Scrooge after shaking hands with him.

The Poor Law.name: The Poor Law
The Poor Law.description: The Poor Law is a system of legislation in operation that Mr. Scrooge references in his inquiry about provisions for the poor.

The Union Workhouses.name: The Union Workhouses
The Union Workhouses.description: The Union workhouses are institutions that are still in operation, as mentioned by the gentleman.

The Treadmill.name: The Treadmill
The Treadmill.description: The Treadmill is a punitive device referenced by Mr. Scrooge in his questioning of social provisions.

Treadmill.name: Treadmill
Treadmill.description: The Treadmill is a penal institution or device that is in full operation, as referenced in the conversation.

Poor Law.name: Poor Law
Poor Law.description: The Poor Law is a legal and administrative system providing relief for the poor, which Scrooge supports and which is in full operation.

Want.name: Want
Want.description: Want refers to poverty and necessity, which is keenly felt during Christmas time. | Want is a girl who symbolizes the societal ill of poverty and need.

Abundance.name: Abundance
Abundance.description: Abundance refers to wealth and plenty, which is contrasted with Want during the holiday season.

Gentlemen.name: Gentlemen
Gentlemen.description: The gentlemen are visitors who approach Scrooge with a charitable purpose but withdraw when Scrooge rejects them.

Lord Mayor.name: Lord Mayor
Lord Mayor.description: The Lord Mayor is a high-ranking official who orders his household to celebrate Christmas in a grand manner. | A person in the stronghold of Mansion House who gave orders to his fifty cooks and butlers to celebrate Christmas appropriately.

Little Tailor.name: Little Tailor
Little Tailor.description: The little tailor is a man who was fined by the Lord Mayor for being drunk and bloodthirsty, but still prepares for Christmas. | A tailor who was fined by the Lord Mayor for being drunk and bloodthirsty, and who stirs up tomorrow's pudding in preparation for Christmas.

Mansion House.name: Mansion House
Mansion House.description: The Mansion House is the official residence of the Lord Mayor. | A stronghold that serves as the residence of the Lord Mayor, where the Christmas orders are given.

St. Dunstan.name: St. Dunstan
St. Dunstan.description: A person of legendary status who is referenced in relation to the cold weather and his potential interaction with the Evil Spirit.

Christmas Carol.name: Christmas Carol
Christmas Carol.description: A song sung by a singer at Scrooge's keyhole, but the singer flees in terror when Scrooge seizes a ruler. | Christmas carol is a song sung by a boy at Scrooge's door, which Scrooge regrets not rewarding.

The Singer.name: The Singer
The Singer.description: A person who sings a Christmas carol at Scrooge's keyhole and flees in terror when Scrooge reacts aggressively.

Camden Town.name: Camden Town
Camden Town.description: The destination of the clerk's run home after work. | Camden Town is the neighborhood where the clerk lives and returns to celebrate Christmas Eve. | Camden Town is the destination for the turkey, where Scrooge intends to have it delivered.

Chambers.name: Chambers
Chambers.description: Chambers are a gloomy suite of rooms in a lowering pile of building where Scrooge lives, once belonging to his deceased partner, Marley. | Chambers are Scrooge's dusty living quarters, where he spends time alone.

The Knocker.name: The Knocker
The Knocker.description: The knocker on Scrooge's door is large and unremarkable, but it transforms into Marley's face. | The knocker is a door knocker that Scrooge admires, noting its honest expression and calling it wonderful.

Marley's Face.name: Marley's Face
Marley's Face.description: Marley's Face appears on the knocker with a dismal light, resembling a bad lobster in a dark cellar.

Genius of the Weather.name: Genius of the Weather
Genius of the Weather.description: The Genius of the Weather is a mythical figure imagined to sit in mournful meditation on the threshold of Scrooge's house.

City of London.name: City of London
City of London.description: The City of London is the area where Scrooge is known to have little fancy about him, compared to its officials.

The Door Knocker.name: The Door Knocker
The Door Knocker.description: The Door Knocker is a physical object on Scrooge's door that briefly transforms into Marley's face.

The House.name: The House
The House.description: The house is the setting where the story unfolds, with multiple floors and a cellar containing wine-merchant's casks, and a staircase wide enough for a hearse.

Echoes.name: Echoes
Echoes.description: Echoes are sounds that resound through the house, which Scrooge is not frightened by.

Wine-Merchant's Cellars.name: Wine-Merchant's Cellars
Wine-Merchant's Cellars.description: The wine-merchant's cellars are located below the house, contributing to the echoes.

Staircase.name: Staircase
Staircase.description: The staircase is wide enough to accommodate a hearse, indicating its large size.

Hearse.name: Hearse
Hearse.description: A hearse is a vehicle that could easily be driven up the staircase, as imagined by the narrator.

Sitting-Room.name: Sitting-Room
Sitting-Room.description: The sitting-room is one of the rooms Scrooge inspects, contains a table, sofa, fire, spoon, and basin. | The sitting-room is the location where Scrooge expresses his joy and interacts with household items after his transformation.

Bedroom.name: Bedroom
Bedroom.description: The bedroom is one of the rooms Scrooge inspects, contains a bed he checks under.

Lumber-Room.name: Lumber-Room
Lumber-Room.description: The lumber-room is a storage room that Scrooge checks, and it appears as usual.

Candle.name: Candle
Candle.description: A candle is Scrooge's source of light as he walks up the stairs.

Fire.name: Fire
Fire.description: A small fire in the grate that Scrooge sits close to in an attempt to warm himself on a bitter night.

Gruel.name: Gruel
Gruel.description: Gruel is a simple porridge-like food that Scrooge prepares and consumes, situated in a saucepan on the hob.

Dressing-Gown.name: Dressing-Gown
Dressing-Gown.description: A dressing-gown hanging in a suspicious attitude, which Scrooge later puts on.

Dutch Tiles.name: Dutch Tiles
Dutch Tiles.description: Quaint tiles in the fireplace depicting biblical scenes, which distract Scrooge's thoughts.

Bell.name: Bell
Bell.description: A disused bell in the room that begins to swing, causing Scrooge astonishment and dread. | A disused bell in Scrooge's room that begins to swing and ring loudly, signaling the ghost's arrival.

Heavy Chain.name: Heavy Chain
Heavy Chain.description: A heavy chain dragged by Marley's Ghost, making a clanking noise as it moves through the house.

Haunted House.name: Haunted House
Haunted House.description: The building where Scrooge lives, which is described as haunted and where the supernatural events occur.

Cellar.name: Cellar
Cellar.description: The wine-merchant's cellar, from which the clanking noise originates before the ghost ascends.

Jacob Marley.name: Jacob Marley
Jacob Marley.description: Jacob Marley is the ghost of Scrooge's former business partner, appearing in chains and transparent form, and insists on being addressed as his former self. | Jacob Marley is the ghost of Scrooge's former business partner. He appears to Scrooge to reveal his identity and engage in a conversation about the reality of his presence. | Jacob Marley is the ghost of Scrooge's former business partner, who wears a heavy chain forged in life. | Jacob Marley is a deceased former business partner of Ebenezer Scrooge, appearing as a ghost who is condemned to wander in perpetual remorse. | Jacob Marley is the ghost of Scrooge's former business partner, who appears to warn Scrooge about his fate. | Jacob Marley is the deceased partner who arranged for the second messenger to visit Scrooge. | Jacob Marley is a deceased former business partner of Scrooge, mentioned in relation to the sexton's spade. | Jacob Marley is a deceased associate of Scrooge whose prediction about the spirits is remembered by Scrooge. | Jacob Marley is mentioned by Scrooge in a prayer of gratitude, indicating a past connection and influence. | Jacob Marley is a deceased business partner of Scrooge, referenced by Scrooge in a moment of gratitude.

Ghost Of Marley.name: Ghost Of Marley
Ghost Of Marley.description: The ghost of Marley is a supernatural being, transparent and wearing chains, who appears before Scrooge to convey a warning.

Chain.name: Chain
Chain.description: The chain is clasped about Marley's middle, made of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks, ledgers, deeds, and heavy purses wrought in steel, symbolizing Marley's earthly attachments.

The Ghost.name: The Ghost
The Ghost.description: The Ghost is a spectre that visits Scrooge, carries a chain, and speaks of the fate of spirits who do not walk abroad in life. | The Ghost, later identified as Jacob Marley, is a spirit condemned to wander the earth and witness what it cannot share. | The Ghost is the spectral apparition of Jacob Marley, conveying messages from other regions and speaking of its own torment and journey. | The Ghost is a spectral figure that appears to Scrooge, lamenting its past life and the misused opportunities, and clanking its chain as a symbol of its remorse. | The Ghost is the spirit of Jacob Marley, appearing to Scrooge in a visible form. | The Ghost is a supernatural entity named Jacob, who visits Scrooge to warn him of his fate and the need for repentance. | A guiding spirit that converses with Scrooge, leading him through visions. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that appears to Scrooge, guiding him on a journey for his reclamation. | The Ghost is a spirit guiding Scrooge through the past, observing his reactions and providing commentary. | The Ghost is a supernatural character who guides Scrooge through memories of the past, explaining the scenes they witness. | The Ghost is a spectral figure who leads Scrooge to a room where Scrooge's younger self is seen, guiding the experience. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that Scrooge observes during his visit. | The Ghost is a spiritual guide who shows Scrooge visions of his past, including scenes with his sister and school. | The Ghost is a supernatural being who guides Scrooge on a journey to revisit his past, stopping at a warehouse and asking Scrooge if he knows it. | The Ghost is a supernatural entity that guides Scrooge through visions and engages in dialogue about the value of Fezziwig's actions. | A supernatural being guiding Scrooge through his past, insisting on showing one more shadow. | The Ghost is a supernatural figure that forces Scrooge to observe another shadow from the past. | The Ghost is a spectral being with a bright light that Scrooge tries to extinguish with an extinguisher-cap. | The Ghost is a supernatural being who transports Scrooge across the sea to observe various scenes, including a ship and Scrooge's nephew's home. | The Ghost is a supernatural being who observes Scrooge's mood and grants him some time to stay, but refuses to let him stay until guests depart. | The Ghost is a spiritual being that accompanies Scrooge, showing scenes of various homes and sickbeds, and visibly ages during their journey. | The Ghost is a spirit that travels with Scrooge, instructs him, and reveals two children from its robe. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that conducts Scrooge through various scenes.

The Chain.name: The Chain
The Chain.description: The Chain is a symbolic object that represents the burdens and consequences of a life lived without compassion. | The Chain is a physical object carried by Marley's ghost, symbolizing his burden and past misdeeds.

The Ward.name: The Ward
The Ward.description: The Ward is implied as a legal jurisdiction or location where proceedings might be justified regarding the Ghost's noise.

Mankind.name: Mankind
Mankind.description: Mankind represents humanity and the common welfare, which Marley claims was his true business.

The Star.name: The Star
The Star.description: The Star is a celestial object that guided the Wise Men, symbolizing hope and spiritual guidance.

Three Spirits.name: Three Spirits
Three Spirits.description: Three Spirits are supernatural entities that will visit Scrooge on consecutive nights as part of his chance to escape the Ghost's fate.

Penance.name: Penance
Penance.description: Penance is described as a significant part of the Ghost's punishment and the reason for its visit to warn Scrooge.

Chance and Hope.name: Chance and Hope
Chance and Hope.description: Chance and hope refer to the possibility of Scrooge escaping the Ghost's fate through the visits of the Three Spirits.

Phantoms.name: Phantoms
Phantoms.description: Phantoms are supernatural beings wandering in the air, wearing chains like Marley's Ghost, moaning, and unable to interfere in human matters.

Chains.name: Chains
Chains.description: Chains are worn by Marley's Ghost and other phantoms as symbols of their imprisonment.

Illustration.name: Illustration
Illustration.description: An illustration depicts the air filled with phantoms wandering in restless haste and moaning.

Spirit Voices.name: Spirit Voices
Spirit Voices.description: Spirit Voices are the ethereal voices of the ghosts that fade away together with them.

Ghost In A White Waistcoat.name: Ghost In A White Waistcoat
Ghost In A White Waistcoat.description: A ghost in a white waistcoat with an iron safe attached to its ankle, who laments being unable to assist a woman with an infant.

Iron Safe.name: Iron Safe
Iron Safe.description: An iron safe is attached to the ankle of one ghost, symbolizing a burden.

The Invisible World.name: The Invisible World
The Invisible World.description: The Invisible World is a realm of spirits and ghosts that Scrooge glimpses.

Wretched Woman.name: Wretched Woman
Wretched Woman.description: A woman with an infant, seen below on a doorstep, whom the ghost in the white waistcoat wishes to assist.

The Clock.name: The Clock
The Clock.description: The Clock is a heavy bell-driven clock in Scrooge's room that unexpectedly continues ringing up to twelve, which Scrooge believes is wrong, possibly due to an icicle in the works.

The Repeater.name: The Repeater
The Repeater.description: The Repeater is Scrooge's pocket watch that also strikes twelve, causing him further confusion about the time.

An Icicle.name: An Icicle
An Icicle.description: An icicle is suggested by Scrooge as a possible cause of the clock malfunctioning.

The Sun.name: The Sun
The Sun.description: The Sun is mentioned by Scrooge as a possible element affected by unusual time, as he wonders if twelve could be noon.

The Weather.name: The Weather
The Weather.description: The Weather is characterized by fog and extreme cold, which affects Scrooge's perception and actions at the window.

First of Exchange.name: First of Exchange
First of Exchange.description: The First of Exchange is a financial document mentioned in Scrooge's thoughts, illustrating his confusion about time and its passage.

United States Security.name: United States Security
United States Security.description: A United States security is a financial instrument that would be of diminished value without a count of days, as referenced in Scrooge's musings.

The Spirit.name: The Spirit
The Spirit.description: The Spirit is a ghostly figure that appears to Scrooge, characterized by its ever-changing form, white hair, and a bright light from its head. | The Spirit is a supernatural figure who sprinkles water and incense on dinners using a torch, and interacts with Scrooge during Christmas celebrations. | The Spirit is a ghostly figure that quotes Scrooge's own words back to him, rebuking him for his callous attitude toward the poor. | The Spirit is a supernatural being guiding Scrooge on a journey to observe Christmas scenes. | The Spirit is a supernatural being that shows Scrooge the children Ignorance and Want and speaks of their significance. | The Spirit is a phantom guide that leads Scrooge through scenes and points to people, providing explanation. | The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come, who guides Scrooge through possible future scenes. | The Spirit is a supernatural guide accompanying Scrooge during the vision. | The Spirit is a supernatural being guiding Scrooge through the vision, pointing towards a churchyard and a specific grave. | A spectral entity that shows the protagonist his past, present, and future, and responds to his pleas for redemption. | The Spirit is a spectral entity that Scrooge encounters, which repulses him and eventually dwindles into a bedpost.

Scrooge's Bedroom.name: Scrooge's Bedroom
Scrooge's Bedroom.description: Scrooge's bedroom is the setting where the supernatural encounter occurs.

The Curtains.name: The Curtains
The Curtains.description: The curtains of Scrooge's bed are drawn aside by the Spirit.

The Holly Branch.name: The Holly Branch
The Holly Branch.description: The Holly Branch is a branch of fresh green holly held by the Spirit.

The Country Road.name: The Country Road
The Country Road.description: The country road is a location where Scrooge and the Ghost arrive, evoking Scrooge's childhood memories.

Market-Town.name: Market-Town
Market-Town.description: A little market-town visible in the distance with a bridge, church, and winding river, where Scrooge spent his childhood.

Winter Day.name: Winter Day
Winter Day.description: A clear, cold winter day with snow on the ground, marking the setting of Scrooge's childhood memory.

Odours.name: Odours
Odours.description: A thousand scents associated with thoughts, hopes, joys, and cares from Scrooge's past, triggering memories.

Boys.name: Boys
Boys.description: A group of boys riding ponies and in carts, shouting and in high spirits, representing Christmas cheer in Scrooge's past. | Boys are the children who delight in watching snow fall from rooftops and creating artificial snowstorms.

The School.name: The School
The School.description: The School is a large, decaying mansion where a solitary child is left neglected by friends. | The school is the location of Scrooge's childhood memories, where he is greeted by the schoolmaster.

The Travellers.name: The Travellers
The Travellers.description: The Travellers are a group of joyful boys who celebrate Christmas and are known by Scrooge.

The Mansion.name: The Mansion
The Mansion.description: The Mansion is a dull red brick building with a cupola and bell, in a state of decay, representing the school. | The mansion is a large, decaying brick house that is the setting of the scene, showing signs of neglect.

Young Scrooge.name: Young Scrooge
Young Scrooge.description: Young Scrooge is the childhood version of Scrooge, shown as a lonely boy reading in a barren classroom.

Ali Baba.name: Ali Baba
Ali Baba.description: Ali Baba is a fictional character from a story that appears outside the window, bringing joy to young Scrooge. | Ali Baba is a character from the story 'Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves', mentioned by Scrooge as a dear old character.

The Classroom.name: The Classroom
The Classroom.description: The classroom is a long, bare room with desks and forms, where young Scrooge is found reading by the fire.

The Poplar Tree.name: The Poplar Tree
The Poplar Tree.description: The poplar tree is a despondent, leafless tree in the yard, its sighs affecting Scrooge's emotions.

The Ass.name: The Ass
The Ass.description: The ass is a donkey laden with wood, led by Ali Baba outside the window.

Valentine.name: Valentine
Valentine.description: Valentine is a character, presumably from a story, who is brother to Orson.

Orson.name: Orson
Orson.description: Orson is a character, described as Valentine's wild brother.

Sultan's Groom.name: Sultan's Groom
Sultan's Groom.description: The Sultan's Groom is a character who was turned upside down by the Genii.

Genii.name: Genii
Genii.description: The Genii are supernatural beings who turned the Sultan's Groom upside down.

Princess.name: Princess
Princess.description: The Princess is a character who was married to the Sultan's Groom.

Parrot.name: Parrot
Parrot.description: The Parrot is a green and yellow bird with a lettuce-like growth on its head, called 'Poor Robin Crusoe' by its owner. | The parrot is a speaking bird that calls out to Robin Crusoe, as quoted in the text.

Robin Crusoe.name: Robin Crusoe
Robin Crusoe.description: Robin Crusoe is a fictional character who sailed around an island and returned home. | Robin Crusoe is a character referenced by the parrot in a dialogue, about whom the parrot asks where he has been after sailing around the island.

Friday.name: Friday
Friday.description: Friday is a character who runs for his life to a little creek. | Friday is a character who runs for his life to a little creek, as mentioned in the text.

Ghost.name: Ghost
Ghost.description: The Ghost is a spirit who shows Scrooge scenes from Christmas past and suggests viewing another Christmas. | The Ghost is a supernatural being that shows Scrooge shadows of the past and is resistant to Scrooge's attempts to extinguish its light. | The Ghost is a jolly giant that appears in Scrooge's room, holding a torch that resembles Plenty's horn, and invites Scrooge to come in. | Ghost is a shorthand reference to the Ghost of Christmas Present in the text. | The Ghost is a spectral being that shows Scrooge two children, representing the moral lesson of the story. | The Ghost is a supernatural entity that guides Scrooge through a vision, revealing the consequences of a man's life.

The Schoolmaster.name: The Schoolmaster
The Schoolmaster.description: The schoolmaster appears in the hall, regards Scrooge with condescension, and shakes his hand. | The schoolmaster is the authority figure at the school, who greets Master Scrooge and his sister and offers them refreshments.

Scrooge's Room.name: Scrooge's Room
Scrooge's Room.description: The room where Scrooge is staying, with panels and windows that deteriorate.

Scrooge's School.name: Scrooge's School
Scrooge's School.description: The school Scrooge attends, from which he is taken home.

The Hall.name: The Hall
The Hall.description: The hall where the schoolmaster appears and calls for Scrooge's box.

Master Scrooge.name: Master Scrooge
Master Scrooge.description: Master Scrooge is the younger version of Scrooge, seen in a childhood memory at school.

Scrooge's Sister.name: Scrooge's Sister
Scrooge's Sister.description: Scrooge's sister is a delicate but warm-hearted child who embraces her brother and takes him home.

The Nephew.name: The Nephew
The Nephew.description: The Nephew is revealed to be the child of Scrooge's sister. | The Nephew is the host at the house and is in the dining-room with his wife when Scrooge visits.

The City.name: The City
The City.description: The city is a bustling place with shops and streets, where Scrooge and the Ghost observe Christmas-time evening. | The city is the location towards which the Spirit stretches his hand, representing society that slanders those who speak of the children. | The City is the location where Scrooge and the Spirit move, appearing to spring up around them as they travel. | The City is the setting where Scrooge and the Phantom appear, surrounded by merchants and business activity.

The Warehouse.name: The Warehouse
The Warehouse.description: The warehouse is a location the Ghost stops at, asking Scrooge if he knows it. | The warehouse is the place where Scrooge was apprenticed and where he revisits his past with the Ghost. | The warehouse is the workplace owned by Fezziwig, which is cleared and transformed into a ball-room for the Christmas Eve celebration.

Old Fezziwig.name: Old Fezziwig
Old Fezziwig.description: Old Fezziwig is a cheerful old gentleman in a Welsh wig, a former employer of Scrooge, who is seen sitting behind a high desk and calls out to his apprentices. | Old Fezziwig is a character who hosts a dance and leads the festivities, including dancing with Mrs. Fezziwig.

Dick.name: Dick
Dick.description: Dick is an apprentice of Fezziwig, described as very much attached to him, and is addressed by Fezziwig during the Christmas Eve preparations. | Dick is a former apprentice of Fezziwig, associated with Scrooge's past.

Ebenezer.name: Ebenezer
Ebenezer.description: Ebenezer is an apprentice of Fezziwig, addressed cheerfully during the Christmas Eve preparations.

Warehouse.name: Warehouse
Warehouse.description: The warehouse is the venue transformed into a ballroom for the Christmas party hosted by Fezziwig.

Fiddler.name: Fiddler
Fiddler.description: The fiddler provides music for the dance, using the desk as an orchestra, and plays energetically.

Miss Fezziwigs.name: Miss Fezziwigs
Miss Fezziwigs.description: The three Miss Fezziwigs are the daughters of Fezziwig, beaming and lovable.

Young Followers.name: Young Followers
Young Followers.description: The six young followers are young men whose hearts were broken by the Miss Fezziwigs.

Young Men and Women.name: Young Men and Women
Young Men and Women.description: The young men and women employed in the business attend the party and participate in the dancing.

Housemaid.name: Housemaid
Housemaid.description: The housemaid is a servant who attends the party with her cousin, the baker.

Baker.name: Baker
Baker.description: The baker is the cousin of the housemaid, attending the party.

Cook.name: Cook
Cook.description: The cook is a servant who attends with her brother's particular friend, the milkman.

Milkman.name: Milkman
Milkman.description: The milkman is the friend of the cook's brother, attending the party.

Boy from Over the Way.name: Boy from Over the Way
Boy from Over the Way.description: The boy from over the way is suspected of not having enough board from his master and hides behind the girl from next door.

Girl from Next Door.name: Girl from Next Door
Girl from Next Door.description: The girl from next door is proved to have had her ears pulled by her mistress.

Christmas Party.name: Christmas Party
Christmas Party.description: A festive dance held in the warehouse, hosted by Fezziwig, featuring music and dancing.

Music-Book.name: Music-Book
Music-Book.description: The music-book is used by the fiddler to play tunes at the party.

The Fiddler.name: The Fiddler
The Fiddler.description: The fiddler is a musician who plays music for the dances, including 'Sir Roger de Coverley', and is described as an 'artful dog'.

Sir Roger de Coverley.name: Sir Roger de Coverley
Sir Roger de Coverley.description: Sir Roger de Coverley is a dance tune played by the fiddler during the evening.

The Dance.name: The Dance
The Dance.description: The dance is a social gathering where numerous couples dance various figures, including the top couple's leads.

Domestic Ball.name: Domestic Ball
Domestic Ball.description: A festive ball hosted by the Fezziwigs, featuring dancing and merry interactions, ending at eleven o'clock.

The Two Apprentices.name: The Two Apprentices
The Two Apprentices.description: The two apprentices are Fezziwig's current apprentices who express gratitude and praise for Fezziwig.

The Party.name: The Party
The Party.description: The party is a Christmas event hosted by Fezziwig, where he bids farewell to guests and receives praise from his apprentices.

Fair Young Girl.name: Fair Young Girl
Fair Young Girl.description: A fair young girl in mourning dress is seen with a younger Scrooge, indicating a past relationship.

He.name: He
He.description: He is an older man, showing signs of care and avarice, with an eager and greedy eye. He is engaged in a conversation with a young girl in mourning.

The Young Girl.name: The Young Girl
The Young Girl.description: A fair young girl in mourning dress, with tears in her eyes, speaking softly about being displaced by another idol. | The Young Girl is a beautiful young girl in the scene who resembles the last person Scrooge saw.

The Golden Idol.name: The Golden Idol
The Golden Idol.description: A metaphorical golden idol representing wealth and greed that has displaced the girl in the man's affections.

Poverty.name: Poverty
Poverty.description: Poverty is discussed as something the world treats with severity, a condition the man fears.

The Contract.name: The Contract
The Contract.description: An old contract, made when both were poor, representing their betrothal or agreement to improve their fortune through industry. | An old agreement made when both were poor, intended to improve their fortune through patient industry.

Gain.name: Gain
Gain.description: Gain is the master passion that has engrossed the man, leading to his obsession with wealth.

The Girl.name: The Girl
The Girl.description: A woman involved in an old romantic contract, now expressing that the nature of the relationship has changed and proposing release.

The Man.name: The Man
The Man.description: A man who was once a boy when the contract was made, now engaged in a conversation about whether he has changed. | The man is a character who, along with Mrs. Dilber, agrees with the woman's statement.

Girl.name: Girl
Girl.description: A woman who has resolved to release her former love from an engagement, citing a change in his nature and principles. | The Girl is one of two children shown to Scrooge, described as wretched and wolfish, symbolizing want.

The Former Love.name: The Former Love
The Former Love.description: A man who was once loved by the Girl but now embodies a changed nature, measuring everything by gain.

The Matron.name: The Matron
The Matron.description: The Matron is a comely matron who sits opposite the young girl, suggesting she is the older version of the girl.

The Daughter.name: The Daughter
The Daughter.description: The Daughter is the daughter of the matron and participates in the children's games, getting pillaged by the young brigands.

The Scene.name: The Scene
The Scene.description: The Scene is a past event showing a comfortable room with a fire, where a family with many children enjoys boisterous games.

The Father.name: The Father
The Father.description: The father is the master of the house who returns home with gifts and is greeted by his family.

The Children.name: The Children
The Children.description: The children are the boisterous group that greets the father and later goes to bed. | The children are descendants of the old man and woman, joining in the Christmas song. | The Children are the mother's children who are playing in the room during the vision.

The Porter.name: The Porter
The Porter.description: The porter is a man laden with Christmas toys and presents who is mobbed by the children.

Christmas Toys.name: Christmas Toys
Christmas Toys.description: Christmas toys are the presents brought by the porter and distributed to the children.

Husband.name: Husband
Husband.description: The husband is Belle's spouse who recognizes Scrooge and reports seeing him alone at his office.

The Extinguisher-Cap.name: The Extinguisher-Cap
The Extinguisher-Cap.description: The Extinguisher-Cap is a device Scrooge uses in an attempt to suppress the Ghost's light.

The Second Spirit.name: The Second Spirit
The Second Spirit.description: The Second Spirit is the second messenger sent to Scrooge, expected to appear after the bell strikes One.

The Bell.name: The Bell
The Bell.description: The Bell is a clock that strikes the hour, signaling the arrival of the spirits.

The Bedroom.name: The Bedroom
The Bedroom.description: The Bedroom is where Scrooge finds himself after the encounter with the Ghost and where he awaits the second spirit.

The Light.name: The Light
The Light.description: The Light is a radiant, ghostly illumination associated with the Ghost and later emanating in Scrooge's room. | The Light is a ruddy glow that surrounds Scrooge, alarming him, and is later revealed to emanate from the adjoining room.

The Room.name: The Room
The Room.description: The Room is Scrooge's own room which has undergone a surprising transformation, adorned with living green and filled with festive foods and a roaring fire. | The room is dark with a bare, uncurtained bed, where the body of the man lies under a ragged sheet.

Living Green.name: Living Green
Living Green.description: Living green consists of holly, mistletoe, and ivy that hang on the walls and ceiling, reflecting light like mirrors.

Food.name: Food
Food.description: A large assortment of food items such as turkeys, geese, game, poultry, brawn, joints of meat, sucking-pigs, sausages, mince-pies, plum-puddings, oysters, chestnuts, apples, oranges, pears, twelfth-cakes, and punch.

Chamber.name: Chamber
Chamber.description: The chamber is the room where the Ghost of Christmas Present sits in state upon a throne of food, dimmed by the steam from the punch.

Holy Wreath.name: Holy Wreath
Holy Wreath.description: A wreath made of holly, adorned with shining icicles, worn on the head of the Ghost of Christmas Present.

Antique Sheath.name: Antique Sheath
Antique Sheath.description: An antique scabbard, rusted and empty, girded around the Ghost's middle, symbolizing peace.

Christmas Morning.name: Christmas Morning
Christmas Morning.description: Christmas morning is the time setting for the scene described, where people are outdoors in the city streets.

City Streets.name: City Streets
City Streets.description: City streets are the urban environment where the characters and activities take place on Christmas morning. | The city streets are the initial setting where Scrooge and the Spirit observe festive preparations in houses.

People.name: People
People.description: People are the residents of the city, engaged in clearing snow and shopping, displaying jovial and eager behavior.

Poulterers' Shops.name: Poulterers' Shops
Poulterers' Shops.description: Poulterers' shops are retail locations selling poultry, still partially open on Christmas morning.

Fruiterers' Shops.name: Fruiterers' Shops
Fruiterers' Shops.description: Fruiterers' shops are retail locations selling fruits, radiant with displays of chestnuts, Spanish onions, pears, apples, grapes, filberts, and Norfolk Biffins.

Grocers' Shops.name: Grocers' Shops
Grocers' Shops.description: Grocers' shops are retail locations offering a wide range of groceries including tea, coffee, raisins, almonds, cinnamon, spices, candied fruits, figs, and French plums, with a bustling atmosphere.

Snow.name: Snow
Snow.description: Snow is the precipitation covering rooftops and ground, being cleared by people and causing a brisk atmosphere.

Mistletoe.name: Mistletoe
Mistletoe.description: Mistletoe is a plant hung up in shops, associated with Christmas decorations and traditions.

Chestnuts.name: Chestnuts
Chestnuts.description: Chestnuts are nuts displayed in large baskets at fruiterers' shops, described with humorous anthropomorphic qualities. | Chestnuts are placed on the fire and sputter and crack noisily as part of the family's Christmas celebration.

Spanish Onions.name: Spanish Onions
Spanish Onions.description: Spanish onions are a vegetable product in the fruiterers' shops, described with humorous characteristics.

Pears.name: Pears
Pears.description: Pears are fruits displayed in blooming pyramids at the fruiterers' shops.

Apples.name: Apples
Apples.description: Apples are fruits displayed in blooming pyramids at the fruiterers' shops.

Grapes.name: Grapes
Grapes.description: Grapes are bunches of fruit dangled from hooks at the fruiterers' shops to entice customers.

Filberts.name: Filberts
Filberts.description: Filberts are nuts piled in the shops, their fragrance evoking walks in the woods.

Norfolk Biffins.name: Norfolk Biffins
Norfolk Biffins.description: Norfolk Biffins are a type of apple, notable for their squab and swarthy appearance, appealing to customers.

Tea.name: Tea
Tea.description: Tea is a beverage ingredient sold in grocers' shops, with a scent that is grateful to the nose.

Coffee.name: Coffee
Coffee.description: Coffee is a beverage ingredient sold in grocers' shops, with a scent that is grateful to the nose.

Grocer.name: Grocer
Grocer.description: The grocer is the shopkeeper of the grocers' shop, described as frank and fresh, with polished hearts on their aprons.

The Grocer.name: The Grocer
The Grocer.description: The grocer is a shopkeeper who, along with his staff, is described as cheerful and busy during the Christmas season.

Customers.name: Customers
Customers.description: Customers are the people shopping in the grocery store, depicted as hurried and eager, causing commotion in their Christmas preparations.

The Bakers.name: The Bakers
The Bakers.description: The bakers are individuals who operate the bakeries where poor revellers send their dinners to be cooked during Christmas.

Christmas Day.name: Christmas Day
Christmas Day.description: Christmas Day is the holiday setting during which the scenes of shopping, cooking, and reconciliation occur. | Christmas Day is the occasion during which the Cratchit family prepares their festive meal and is visited by the Ghost. | Christmas Day is the holiday during which the Cratchit family shares their toast and expresses their feelings about Mr. Scrooge. | Christmas Day is a holiday that is repeatedly mentioned by Bob Cratchit as a reason to temper Mrs. Cratchit's harsh words about Scrooge. | Christmas Day is the holiday that Scrooge discovers it is, bringing him joy and relief.

The Torch.name: The Torch
The Torch.description: The torch is a special item held by the Spirit that sprinkles water to restore good humor and incense on dinners.

The Seventh Day.name: The Seventh Day
The Seventh Day.description: The Seventh Day is a concept referring to the Sabbath, which Scrooge accuses the Spirit's name and family of being used to close places of dining, thereby depriving the poor of their means of dining.

Bob Cratchit's Dwelling.name: Bob Cratchit's Dwelling
Bob Cratchit's Dwelling.description: Bob Cratchit's Dwelling is the home of Scrooge's clerk, which the Spirit blesses with sprinklings from his torch.

The Poor.name: The Poor
The Poor.description: The Poor refers to the impoverished individuals who most need kindly given dinners and whose innocent enjoyment is being restricted by the closing of places on the Seventh Day.

Master Peter Cratchit.name: Master Peter Cratchit
Master Peter Cratchit.description: Master Peter Cratchit is the eldest son of the Cratchit family who tends to the potatoes and is admired by his younger siblings. | Master Peter Cratchit is a son in the Cratchit family who helps fetch the goose and mashes the potatoes.

Cratchit Family.name: Cratchit Family
Cratchit Family.description: The Cratchit family consists of Bob, Mrs. Cratchit, Belinda, Peter, Tiny Tim, Martha, and two younger children, observed during Christmas preparations. | The Cratchit family is the family unit gathered for a Christmas dinner, including Bob, Mrs. Cratchit, and their children. | The Cratchit family consists of Bob, Mrs. Cratchit, Peter, Tiny Tim, and other children. They are depicted as a close, loving family sharing grief and joy together. | The Cratchit Family includes Bob Cratchit, Mrs. Cratchit, their daughters, the two young Cratchits, and Peter, who all express love and remembrance.

The Two Young Cratchits.name: The Two Young Cratchits
The Two Young Cratchits.description: Two young children in the Cratchit family who are energetic and participate in the merriment, announcing Martha's arrival and helping Tiny Tim. | The Two Young Cratchits are the younger children of the Cratchit family who help with chores and escort Tiny Tim. | The two young Cratchits are children of the Cratchit family who become livid at the supposition that the pudding might be stolen.

The Cratchit Family.name: The Cratchit Family
The Cratchit Family.description: The Cratchit family is a close-knit family celebrating Christmas together, consisting of Bob, Mrs. Cratchit, Tiny Tim, Martha, Peter, Belinda, and the younger children. | The Cratchit family includes Bob, his wife, and their children, including Tiny Tim, Peter, and Martha; they are poor but happy. | The Cratchit family includes the mother, daughters, and sons, who are depicted in a quiet moment.

Cratchit.name: Cratchit
Cratchit.description: Cratchit is a family member who prepared the gravy for the goose dinner.

Master Peter.name: Master Peter
Master Peter.description: Master Peter is a child in the Cratchit family who mashed the potatoes with great vigour. | Master Peter is the eldest son of the Cratchit family, who contemplates investments from a prospective income.

Miss Belinda.name: Miss Belinda
Miss Belinda.description: Miss Belinda is a child in the Cratchit family who sweetened the applesauce and later changed the plates.

Martha.name: Martha
Martha.description: Martha is a member of the Cratchit family who dusted the hot plates for the meal. | Martha is a poor apprentice at a milliner's and the daughter of Bob Cratchit, who shares details about her work.

Bob.name: Bob
Bob.description: Bob is a member of the Cratchit family who sat next to Tiny Tim and expressed admiration for the goose. | Bob is a family man who serves hot drinks from a jug, proposes a Christmas toast to his family, and cares deeply for his son Tiny Tim. | Bob is a family man who works and shares news about Mr. Scrooge's nephew's kindness with his family. | Bob is an employee who arrives late and apologizes to Scrooge.

The two young Cratchits.name: The two young Cratchits
The two young Cratchits.description: The two young Cratchits are children in the Cratchit family who set chairs and crammed spoons into their mouths, then excited Tiny Tim.

The Goose.name: The Goose
The Goose.description: The goose is the main dish of the Cratchit family's dinner, praised for its tenderness, flavour, size, and cheapness. | The goose is a food item being eaten by the Cratchit family, and its consumption is part of the context in which the pudding is served.

The Pudding.name: The Pudding
The Pudding.description: The pudding is a dessert that Mrs. Cratchit prepared and brought in after the goose, causing anxiety about its condition.

The Christmas Pudding.name: The Christmas Pudding
The Christmas Pudding.description: The Christmas pudding is a dessert made by Mrs. Cratchit, described as speckled, hard, firm, and blazing with brandy and holly.

The Back-Yard Wall.name: The Back-Yard Wall
The Back-Yard Wall.description: The back-yard wall is the boundary over which someone might have climbed to steal the pudding.

Christmas Pudding.name: Christmas Pudding
Christmas Pudding.description: The Christmas pudding is a hard, firm pudding served with ignited brandy and holly, considered a great success by Bob Cratchit.

Christmas Dinner.name: Christmas Dinner
Christmas Dinner.description: The Christmas dinner is the occasion during which the Cratchit family gathers and celebrates with pudding and a toast.

The Jug's Compound.name: The Jug's Compound
The Jug's Compound.description: The compound in the jug is a drink served to the family, considered perfect after tasting and held in tumblers and a custard cup.

Crutch.name: Crutch
Crutch.description: A crutch is used by Tiny Tim; in the vision, a crutch without an owner is preserved, symbolizing the child's death.

The Poor Man's Child.name: The Poor Man's Child
The Poor Man's Child.description: The Poor Man's Child is a child mentioned by the Spirit as an example of a life that might be deemed worthless by Scrooge's standards.

The Founder of the Feast.name: The Founder of the Feast
The Founder of the Feast.description: The Founder of the Feast is the title Bob Cratchit gives to Mr. Scrooge during a Christmas toast, despite Scrooge's negative traits.

The Cratchit Children.name: The Cratchit Children
The Cratchit Children.description: The Cratchit children participate in the Christmas toast and show a lack of heartiness when drinking to Scrooge's health.

Spirit.name: Spirit
Spirit.description: The Spirit is a supernatural guide accompanying Scrooge, whose torch sprinkles brightness, making the family appear happier. | The Spirit is a ghostly entity representing the Ghost of the Future, whose presence instills fear in Scrooge and guides him silently. | The Spirit is a phantom that guides Scrooge through the scene. | The Spirit is a supernatural entity that Scrooge confronts, leading to his emotional release and change of heart.

The Song.name: The Song
The Song.description: A song about a lost child travelling in the snow, sung by Tiny Tim.

Moor.name: Moor
Moor.description: The moor is a bleak, desert-like place where miners live and where the Spirit takes Scrooge.

Miners.name: Miners
Miners.description: Miners are people who live in huts on the moor and work underground; they know the Spirit.

Miners' Hut.name: Miners' Hut
Miners' Hut.description: The miners' hut is a humble dwelling with a glowing fire where a cheerful family gathers.

Holiday Attire.name: Holiday Attire
Holiday Attire.description: Holiday attire refers to the gaily decorated clothing worn by the people in the miners' hut during the Christmas gathering.

The Old Man.name: The Old Man
The Old Man.description: The old man is an elderly person in the hut, singing a Christmas song to his family. | The old man is a character who manages the fire and lamp in the parlour, and participates in the conversation.

The Old Woman.name: The Old Woman
The Old Woman.description: The old woman is the wife of the old man, part of the family gathered around the fire. | The old woman is one of the people grouped about the spoil, who laughs and comments on how the dead man frightened others away to profit them.

The Lighthouse.name: The Lighthouse
The Lighthouse.description: A lighthouse built on a reef, where two men watch the light and celebrate Christmas.

The Ship.name: The Ship
The Ship.description: A ship where the crew members hum Christmas tunes and have Christmas thoughts. | The ship is a vessel at sea where the Ghost and Scrooge observe the crew celebrating Christmas in their own way.

The Two Lighthouse Keepers.name: The Two Lighthouse Keepers
The Two Lighthouse Keepers.description: Two men who watch the light in the lighthouse and exchange Christmas greetings.

The Helmsman.name: The Helmsman
The Helmsman.description: The helmsman is the person at the wheel on the ship, part of the crew.

The Lookout.name: The Lookout
The Lookout.description: The lookout is positioned at the bow of the ship, among the crew.

The Officers.name: The Officers
The Officers.description: The officers are responsible for the watch on the ship, part of the crew.

Scrooge's Niece.name: Scrooge's Niece
Scrooge's Niece.description: Scrooge's niece by marriage is present at the Christmas gathering, laughs heartily, and responds indignantly to Fred's remarks about Scrooge. | Scrooge's niece is Fred's wife, who is described as very pretty and indignant at Scrooge's views. | Scrooge's niece is a relative of Scrooge who comments on his wealth and lack of patience with him, and she and others judge that he loses a very good dinner. | Scrooge's niece is the wife of Scrooge's nephew who encourages her husband to continue speaking and shares in the merriment. | Scrooge's niece is the hostess of the Christmas gathering and a skilled harp player. | Scrooge's niece is a character at the party who sits in a comfortable corner and participates in games, often defeating her sisters.

The Fire.name: The Fire
The Fire.description: The fire is a source of light and warmth built by two men on shore, shedding a ray of brightness on the sea.

The Two Men.name: The Two Men
The Two Men.description: Two men on the shore build a fire and exchange Merry Christmas wishes over a can of grog, representing the spirit of Christmas in remote places.

Wealth.name: Wealth
Wealth.description: Wealth is discussed in the context of Scrooge's riches being of no use to him because he does not use them for good.

Scrooge's Niece's Sisters.name: Scrooge's Niece's Sisters
Scrooge's Niece's Sisters.description: Scrooge's niece's sisters are relatives of Scrooge who agree with the niece's negative opinion of Scrooge.

Topper.name: Topper
Topper.description: Topper is a bachelor who expresses a view on marriage and has his eye on one of Scrooge's niece's sisters. | Topper is a guest at the Christmas party, known for his bass singing and his playful pursuit of the plump sister during games. | Topper is a character in a Christmas party scene, portrayed as a blind man who uses his supposed blindness to pursue a plump sister. | Topper is a character who could attest to the sharpness of the sisters in games. | Topper is a guest at the party, arriving after Fred.

Plump Sister.name: Plump Sister
Plump Sister.description: Plump sister is one of Scrooge's niece's sisters, who blushes when Topper makes a comment about bachelors. | The plump sister is a female character at the party whom Topper pursues, and she protests his unfair advances. | The Plump Sister is a participant who successfully guesses the answer in the game Yes and No.

Office.name: Office
Office.description: Office is Scrooge's workplace, described as mouldy, where Scrooge spends time in his own thoughts.

Fifty Pounds.name: Fifty Pounds
Fifty Pounds.description: Fifty pounds is a sum of money that Scrooge's nephew hopes Scrooge might leave to his poor clerk.

Uncle Scrooge.name: Uncle Scrooge
Uncle Scrooge.description: Uncle Scrooge is a miserly old man, the uncle of the narrator's wife, who is invited to Christmas dinner every year despite his grumpy demeanor.

The Plump Sister.name: The Plump Sister
The Plump Sister.description: The plump sister is a young woman at the Christmas party, wearing a lace tucker, who is pursued by Topper during the games. | The plump sister is a guest at the party, arriving after Topper.

The Christmas Party.name: The Christmas Party
The Christmas Party.description: The Christmas party is a festive gathering hosted by Scrooge's nephew and niece, featuring music, games, and merriment.

Harp.name: Harp
Harp.description: The harp is an instrument played by Scrooge's niece during the party.

The Air.name: The Air
The Air.description: The air is a simple musical tune that Scrooge's niece plays, familiar to the child who fetched Scrooge from boarding school.

The Boarding School.name: The Boarding School
The Boarding School.description: The boarding school is the place from which the child fetched Scrooge, as reminded by the Ghost of Christmas Past.

Ghost Of Christmas Present.name: Ghost Of Christmas Present
Ghost Of Christmas Present.description: The Ghost of Christmas Present is a spectral figure who shows Scrooge the party scene and is aware of Topper's deception. | The Ghost of Christmas Present is a spirit that sat in the corner of Scrooge's sitting-room.

Blind Man's Buff.name: Blind Man's Buff
Blind Man's Buff.description: Blind Man's Buff is a party game in which one player is blindfolded and tries to catch others, which Topper uses to pursue the plump sister.

How, When, And Where.name: How, When, And Where
How, When, And Where.description: How, When, and Where is a game played at the party, in which Scrooge's niece excels.

Forfeits.name: Forfeits
Forfeits.description: Forfeits is a game played at the party, involving penalties for mistakes, and Scrooge's niece participates.

Whitechapel Needle.name: Whitechapel Needle
Whitechapel Needle.description: A sharp needle from Whitechapel, used metaphorically to describe Scrooge's sharpness in guessing.

Yes and No.name: Yes and No
Yes and No.description: Yes and No is a game played where one person thinks of something and others ask questions to guess it.

How, When, and Where.name: How, When, and Where
How, When, and Where.description: How, When, and Where is a game in which the plump sister excels and beats her sisters.

Mulled Wine.name: Mulled Wine
Mulled Wine.description: Mulled wine is a drink prepared by Fred and the company for the toast to Scrooge.

Twelfth-Night Party.name: Twelfth-Night Party
Twelfth-Night Party.description: A children's party during Twelfth-Night that Scrooge and the Ghost attend, after which Scrooge notices the Ghost's hair has turned grey. | An event attended by Scrooge and the Ghost, where the Ghost's gray hair is first noticed.

Two Children.name: Two Children
Two Children.description: Two children, described as wretched and miserable, are brought out from under the Ghost's robe.

Almshouse.name: Almshouse
Almshouse.description: A location the spirit visits to leave his blessing and teach Scrooge his precepts.

Hospital.name: Hospital
Hospital.description: A location the spirit visits to leave his blessing and teach Scrooge his precepts.

Gaol.name: Gaol
Gaol.description: A location the spirit visits to leave his blessing and teach Scrooge his precepts.

Boy.name: Boy
Boy.description: The Boy is one of two children shown to Scrooge, described as wretched and wolfish, symbolizing ignorance. | A boy in Sunday clothes who is addressed by Scrooge, possibly loitering in the area. | The boy is a young character who is sent by Scrooge to purchase a turkey and bring the poulterer's man back.

Humanity.name: Humanity
Humanity.description: Humanity represents the collective condition of people, which is perverted in the children, as described by the Spirit.

Ignorance.name: Ignorance
Ignorance.description: Ignorance is a boy who symbolizes the societal ill of ignorance, described as having doom written on his brow unless erased.

The Last Spirit.name: The Last Spirit
The Last Spirit.description: The Last Spirit, also called the Phantom, is a solemn, hooded ghost that approaches Scrooge after the twelfth bell.

Prisons.name: Prisons
Prisons.description: Prisons are institutions mentioned by the Spirit as a rebuke to Scrooge's earlier words, symbolizing the lack of refuge for the poor.

Workhouses.name: Workhouses
Workhouses.description: Workhouses are institutions mentioned by the Spirit as a rebuke to Scrooge's earlier words, symbolizing the lack of real resource for the needy.

Old Jacob Marley.name: Old Jacob Marley
Old Jacob Marley.description: Old Jacob Marley is a deceased person who predicted the coming of the Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come to Scrooge.

Ghost of the Future.name: Ghost of the Future
Ghost of the Future.description: The Ghost of the Future is a spectral being that Scrooge addresses, embodying the future and leading him through the City.

The Phantom.name: The Phantom
The Phantom.description: The Phantom is a spirit that leads Scrooge through the city, pointing to a group of business men. | The Phantom is a supernatural entity that Scrooge glances towards, likely the spirit guiding him through the scene. | The Phantom is a supernatural spirit that reveals scenes to Scrooge, using its dark robe to unveil a room with a family.

The Merchants.name: The Merchants
The Merchants.description: The merchants are business people in the City who are discussing the death of a man, noting that he has left money to his company.

The Business Men.name: The Business Men
The Business Men.description: The business men are a group of merchants in the City who are particularly engaged in conversation about a man's death and his money.

The Dead Man.name: The Dead Man
The Dead Man.description: The dead man is the subject of the business men's conversation, who died last night and left his money to his company. | The dead man is a deceased individual whose belongings are being distributed among the speakers, and who is criticized for his miserly nature. | The dead man is the subject of the dialogue and the body that lies plundered and bereft on a bare bed, unwatched and unwept. | The Dead Man is the departed individual whose life and death are the focus of Scrooge's vision. | The Dead Man is the person whose death is central to the scene. He was ill and dying when Scrooge tried to see him, and his death brings relief to Caroline and her husband.

The Man with the Large Chin.name: The Man with the Large Chin
The Man with the Large Chin.description: The man with the large chin is one of the business men who reveals he knows little about the dead man's affairs.

The Red-Faced Gentleman.name: The Red-Faced Gentleman
The Red-Faced Gentleman.description: The red-faced gentleman is one of the business men who asks about the dead man's money.

Man With Large Chin.name: Man With Large Chin
Man With Large Chin.description: The man with the large chin is a speaker in the conversation who jokes about the funeral and claims to be the deceased's most particular friend.

Gentleman With Excrescence.name: Gentleman With Excrescence
Gentleman With Excrescence.description: The gentleman with the excrescence on his nose is a speaker who agrees to attend the funeral if a lunch is provided.

The Deceased.name: The Deceased
The Deceased.description: The deceased is the individual whose funeral is being discussed, left to his company.

First Businessman.name: First Businessman
First Businessman.description: First Businessman is a wealthy and important man of business who engages in a brief conversation with another businessman.

Second Businessman.name: Second Businessman
Second Businessman.description: Second Businessman is also wealthy and important, and reports the news about old Scratch's demise.

Christmas-Time.name: Christmas-Time
Christmas-Time.description: Christmas-Time is referenced as a season, with the weather being described as 'seasonable'.

Jacob.name: Jacob
Jacob.description: Scrooge's former business partner, whose death is referenced in the scene.

The Shadow of Scrooge.name: The Shadow of Scrooge
The Shadow of Scrooge.description: Scrooge's future self that he expects to see in the scene but does not find.

The Porch.name: The Porch
The Porch.description: The entrance to the place where people gathered, indicating a public area associated with Scrooge's habitual presence.

Phantom.name: Phantom
Phantom.description: The Phantom is an ethereal being accompanying Scrooge, with an outstretched hand and the ability to show scenes of the town. | The Phantom is a ghostly being who shows Scrooge the scene of a dead body, pointing steadily to the head of the corpse.

Unseen Eyes.name: Unseen Eyes
Unseen Eyes.description: The Unseen Eyes are the perceiving entities associated with the Phantom, looking at Scrooge keenly.

District.name: District
District.description: The District is an obscure, impoverished, and crime-ridden part of the town that Scrooge visited for the first time.

Low-Browed Shop.name: Low-Browed Shop
Low-Browed Shop.description: The Low-Browed Shop is a place where iron, rags, bottles, bones, and greasy offal were bought, and where the old man works.

Old Joe.name: Old Joe
Old Joe.description: Old Joe is a grey-haired, nearly seventy-year-old man who deals in the wares of the shop, smoking his pipe by a charcoal stove. | Old Joe is an old man who smokes a pipe and owns the shop where the three characters meet. | Old Joe is the person addressed by the woman to open a bundle and assess its value, indicating he is involved in the buying or valuing of stolen goods. | Old Joe is a buyer who purchases goods from women, noting their accounts on the wall and bargaining over prices. | Old Joe is a person who produces a flannel bag with money and tells out the gains of the group on the ground.

Charwoman.name: Charwoman
Charwoman.description: The Charwoman is the first woman who entered the shop with a heavy bundle, identitified by the others as the first arrival.

Laundress.name: Laundress
Laundress.description: The Laundress is the second woman who entered the shop with a heavy bundle, also surprised at the encounter.

Undertaker's Man.name: Undertaker's Man
Undertaker's Man.description: The Undertaker's Man is a man in faded black who entered the shop last, startled by the sight of the others.

The Charwoman.name: The Charwoman
The Charwoman.description: The Charwoman is the first of the three who entered the shop, and is described as being the first to be let alone.

The Laundress.name: The Laundress
The Laundress.description: The Laundress is the second of the three who entered the shop, and is described as being the second to be let alone.

The Undertaker's Man.name: The Undertaker's Man
The Undertaker's Man.description: The Undertaker's Man is the third of the three who entered the shop, and is described as being the third to be let alone.

The Parlour.name: The Parlour
The Parlour.description: The parlour is the space behind the screen of rags in old Joe's shop, where the three characters go. | The parlour is the space behind the screen of rags where the characters gather and converse.

The Shop.name: The Shop
The Shop.description: The shop is old Joe's place of business, with a door that skreeks and rusty hinges.

The Bundle.name: The Bundle
The Bundle.description: The bundle is a collection of items that the woman wants Old Joe to appraise, likely stolen from the dead man's house.

Man In Faded Black.name: Man In Faded Black
Man In Faded Black.description: A man dressed in faded black clothing who presents a small collection of valuable items for sale.

Plunder.name: Plunder
Plunder.description: Plunder refers to the stolen or found items brought by the man in faded black, including seals, a pencil-case, sleeve-buttons, and a brooch.

Household Items.name: Household Items
Household Items.description: Household items include sheets, towels, wearing apparel, silver teaspoons, sugar-tongs, and boots that Mrs. Dilber brought.

Dilber.name: Dilber
Dilber.description: Dilber is a woman who engages in selling items, including sheets, towels, clothing, silver teaspoons, and boots, to old Joe.

The First Woman.name: The First Woman
The First Woman.description: The first woman is a seller who brings a bundle containing bed-curtains taken from a deceased man's bed, along with blankets and oil.

Bed-Curtains.name: Bed-Curtains
Bed-Curtains.description: Bed-curtains are a large heavy roll of dark stuff that the first woman sells to old Joe, having taken them down from the deceased man's bed. | Bed-curtains are household items that Scrooge identifies as intact, symbolizing his opportunity to change the future.

Silver Teaspoons.name: Silver Teaspoons
Silver Teaspoons.description: Silver teaspoons are among the items sold by Dilber to old Joe.

Sugar-Tongs.name: Sugar-Tongs
Sugar-Tongs.description: Sugar-tongs are among the items sold by Dilber to old Joe.

Blankets.name: Blankets
Blankets.description: Blankets belong to the deceased man and are part of the bundle brought by the first woman.

Oil.name: Oil
Oil.description: Oil is a substance that the first woman warns Joe not to drop on the blankets.

The Deceased Man.name: The Deceased Man
The Deceased Man.description: The deceased man is the former owner of the bed-curtains, blankets, and other items sold by the first woman. | The Deceased Man is the former owner of the blankets and shirt; his body was dressed in the shirt, but the woman removed it.

The Shirt.name: The Shirt
The Shirt.description: The Shirt is a fine, hole-free garment that belonged to the deceased man. The woman removed it from his body before burial to prevent waste.

The Blankets.name: The Blankets
The Blankets.description: The Blankets belong to the deceased man and are being preserved, with the woman cautioning Joe not to spill oil on them.

Death.name: Death
Death.description: Death is portrayed as a powerful, cold, and dreadful force, but one that cannot diminish the goodness of a person's deeds.

The Mother.name: The Mother
The Mother.description: The Mother is a woman who is anxiously awaiting someone, likely connected to the dead man's death.

The Dark House.name: The Dark House
The Dark House.description: The Dark House is the empty room where the dead man lies, a place of death and desolation.

Caroline's Husband.name: Caroline's Husband
Caroline's Husband.description: Caroline's husband is a young man with a careworn and depressed face, who brings news of the man's death and reveals the possibility of hope due to the death.

Peter.name: Peter
Peter.description: Peter is a child in the Cratchit household who is reading a book. | One of Bob's children, who participates in the family conversation.

The Debt.name: The Debt
The Debt.description: A monetary debt that Caroline and her companion may owe, which might be transferred to a new creditor.

Sunday.name: Sunday
Sunday.description: Sunday is mentioned as a day when the sewing work would be completed, indicating a deadline or a special day in the household.

The Child.name: The Child
The Child.description: Bob Cratchit's child, referred to affectionately as 'My little child!' The child is present in a room upstairs, with a chair placed nearby.

The Green Place.name: The Green Place
The Green Place.description: A green place that Bob Cratchit visited and describes as refreshing, promising to walk there on Sundays.

Child.name: Child
Child.description: Bob's child, who is ill but present in the room upstairs.

Mr. Scrooge's Nephew.name: Mr. Scrooge's Nephew
Mr. Scrooge's Nephew.description: A kindly gentleman who met Bob on the street and showed concern for Bob's distress.

The Cratchit Daughters.name: The Cratchit Daughters
The Cratchit Daughters.description: The Cratchit daughters are the children of the Cratchit family who join in the family conversations and expressions of remembrance.

The Benefactor.name: The Benefactor
The Benefactor.description: The Benefactor is an unnamed gentleman who gave his card to Bob and expressed sympathy for the family, showing kindness.

Spirit of Tiny Tim.name: Spirit of Tiny Tim
Spirit of Tiny Tim.description: The Spirit of Tiny Tim is the essence of Tiny Tim, considered to be from God, a symbol of innocence and goodness.

The Churchyard.name: The Churchyard
The Churchyard.description: The churchyard is a burial ground where the grave of a man is located, overrun with grass and weeds.

The Grave.name: The Grave
The Grave.description: The grave is the specific burial site pointed out by the Spirit, which Scrooge approaches trembling. | The grave is Scrooge's own neglected burial site, pointed to by the Ghost, bearing his name.

The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.name: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come
The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come.description: The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come is a spectral entity that shows Scrooge his future grave, pointing down to it silently.

The Shadow of the Things.name: The Shadow of the Things
The Shadow of the Things.description: The shadows of the things that Will be or May be, representing possible future events.

Christmas Time.name: Christmas Time
Christmas Time.description: Christmas Time is referenced as a period of celebration and spiritual significance, praised by Scrooge.

The Bedpost.name: The Bedpost
The Bedpost.description: The Bedpost is the object that the Spirit transforms into, revealing Scrooge's own bed and room.

Saucepan.name: Saucepan
Saucepan.description: The saucepan is a household item that Scrooge notices in the fireplace area, part of his surroundings in his joy.

Ghost Of Jacob Marley.name: Ghost Of Jacob Marley
Ghost Of Jacob Marley.description: The Ghost of Jacob Marley is a spirit that entered through the door in Scrooge's sitting-room.

Wandering Spirits.name: Wandering Spirits
Wandering Spirits.description: The Wandering Spirits are spirits that Scrooge saw through the window of his sitting-room.

Scrooge's Sitting-Room.name: Scrooge's Sitting-Room
Scrooge's Sitting-Room.description: Scrooge's sitting-room is the room where Scrooge observes the locations associated with the spirits and expresses his joyful realization.

The Boy.name: The Boy
The Boy.description: The Boy is a young lad in Sunday clothes whom Scrooge questions about the day, and who knows the location of a poulterer's shop. | The boy is a young lad who knows the poulterer's location and confirms the turkey is still hanging there. | The boy is a young individual who is recompensed by Scrooge, likely for delivering the turkey.

The Spirits.name: The Spirits
The Spirits.description: The Spirits are supernatural beings who, in one night, have brought about Scrooge's transformation.

The Poulterer's.name: The Poulterer's
The Poulterer's.description: The Poulterer's is a shop on the next street, whose location Scrooge asks the boy about.

Poulterer's Shop.name: Poulterer's Shop
Poulterer's Shop.description: The poulterer's shop is located at the corner of the next street but one, where the prize turkey is sold.

Prize Turkey.name: Prize Turkey
Prize Turkey.description: The prize turkey is a large turkey, as big as the boy, hanging at the poulterer's and intended for purchase by Scrooge.

Turkey.name: Turkey
Turkey.description: The turkey is a large bird purchased by Scrooge to be sent to Bob Cratchit's family as an anonymous gift.

Joe Miller.name: Joe Miller
Joe Miller.description: Joe Miller is a person referenced by Scrooge as a comparison for the joke of sending the turkey to Bob's.

Poulterer's Man.name: Poulterer's Man
Poulterer's Man.description: The poulterer's man is the delivery person expected to bring the turkey to Scrooge.

Knocker.name: Knocker
Knocker.description: The knocker is a door knocker that Scrooge admires, expressing love for it after noticing it.

Bob Cratchit's House.name: Bob Cratchit's House
Bob Cratchit's House.description: Bob Cratchit's house is the destination where the turkey is to be delivered.

The Turkey.name: The Turkey
The Turkey.description: The turkey is a large bird that Scrooge buys and plans to send to Camden Town, noting it is too big to carry.

The Cab.name: The Cab
The Cab.description: The cab is a vehicle hired by Scrooge to transport the turkey to Camden Town.

The Ghost of Christmas Present.name: The Ghost of Christmas Present
The Ghost of Christmas Present.description: The Ghost of Christmas Present is a spirit that appeared to Scrooge earlier, and Scrooge recalls seeing people pouring forth as with this ghost.

The Girl (Maid).name: The Girl (Maid)
The Girl (Maid).description: The Girl is a servant in the nephew's household who answers the door and directs Scrooge to the dining-room.

The Dining Room.name: The Dining Room
The Dining Room.description: The Dining Room is the room in the nephew's house where the family is gathered and the table is set.

The Table.name: The Table
The Table.description: The Table is spread out in great array, indicating a formal meal setting in the dining room.

Fred's Wife.name: Fred's Wife
Fred's Wife.description: Fred's wife is Scrooge's niece by marriage, who is startled by Scrooge's sudden appearance.

Dining Room.name: Dining Room
Dining Room.description: The dining room is where the family is gathered, the table spread in great array for dinner.

Dinner.name: Dinner
Dinner.description: Dinner is the social gathering at Fred's home to which Scrooge has come.

The Office.name: The Office
The Office.description: The office is where the main character arrives early to catch Bob Cratchit coming late.

Total-Abstinence Principle.name: Total-Abstinence Principle
Total-Abstinence Principle.description: The Total-Abstinence Principle is a moral guideline that Scrooge follows after his transformation.

Spirits.name: Spirits
Spirits.description: Spirits are supernatural beings that Scrooge had no further intercourse with after his transformation.
